Tom — thanks for the note and the redlines. We're reviewing with legal and pricing; I wanted to outline the three practical approaches we typically propose so you have context before we send formal counter language: 

1) Annualized cap (rolling 12-month lookback): cap = greater of $X or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months. Pros: aligns with annual spend and limits one-off exposure spikes. Cons: can be higher for customers with lumpy spend.
2) Term-aggregate cap: cap = 2x total fees paid under the Order Form over the contract term. Pros: predictable total exposure; simpler for accounting. Cons: penalizes growth (cap not increasing with new spend).
3) Hybrid floor/ceiling: per-year floor with overall aggregate ceiling (e.g., 1x fees/year with a term cap of 3x). Pros: balances growth protection and total exposure limitation.

For Aster's ask on privacy fines carve-out: we usually push to limit the carve-out to regulatory fines that arise directly from Redwood's breach of obligations (narrowly tailored) and exclude third-party vendor fines.

I'll send a short counter-proposal document today with sample language for each option so legal can pick.

- Soojin

We've also included a short worked example for a customer whose monthly spend grows from $20k to $80k over 12 months to illustrate how a rolling 12-month cap moves vs a static term cap.

To answer your specific questions: 
1) Redwood can accept regulatory fines limited to "amounts finally awarded by a competent judicial authority" and arising from "Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct" — but those amounts would be included within the selected liability cap (we cannot accept an unlimited carve-out).
2) See the attached worked example (in the PDF) — the rolling cap smooths spikes but will scale up with growth; term-aggregate stays fixed and can be lower than a rolling cap for rapidly growing customers.

Next steps: please confirm which option Aster prefers and whether your GC will accept the proposed narrow carve-out language. If Aster prefers the term-aggregate, we will propose an indexing mechanic at renewal to avoid freezing the cap as spend grows.
